slot.brief: find the domain of a function involving a square root and a denominator; decide via inequalities/intersection of conditions

stem: The domain of the real valued function f(x) = sqrt((x^2 - 4x + 3)/(x^2 - 9)) is

verdicts.working: Factor the radicand as ((x−1)(x−3))/((x−3)(x+3)); exclude x=±3. A sign chart gives nonnegative values on (−∞,−3), [1,3), and (3,∞).

working:
Factor numerator and denominator: (x-1)(x-3)/((x-3)(x+3)). The original denominator is zero at x = -3, 3, so exclude both. For x not equal to -3, 3, the quotient is (x-1)/(x+3). Need (x-1)/(x+3) >= 0. Critical points are -3 and 1. Sign is positive on (-infinity, -3) and (1, infinity), negative on (-3, 1), and zero at x = 1. Excluding x = 3 gives (-infinity, -3) U [1, 3) U (3, infinity).

Independent check: Factor the radicand as ((x−1)(x−3))/((x−3)(x+3)); exclude x=±3. A sign chart gives nonnegative values on (−∞,−3), [1,3), and (3,∞).
solution:
For the square root to be real, the radicand must be nonnegative, and the original denominator requires $x\ne\pm3$.
$$\frac{(x-1)(x-3)}{(x-3)(x+3)}=\frac{x-1}{x+3}\ge0,\qquad x\ne\pm3.$$
A sign check gives $(-\infty,-3)\cup[1,\infty)$; excluding $x=3$ gives $(-\infty,-3)\cup[1,3)\cup(3,\infty)$.
